project.name: GhostKey
project.currentFocus: Hybrid Autokey coursework lab plus bounded classroom automated cryptanalysis suite.
durableFacts: MVP direction is a single Next.js App Router application with React, Tailwind CSS, Vercel deployment, and browser Web Workers for heavy cryptanalysis.
MVP has no custom backend, no database, and no auth unless saved labs, classroom management, accounts, sharing, or server-side processing are approved later.
Initial implementation includes a Next.js 16.2.4 App Router app with React 19.2.5, Tailwind 4.2.4, TypeScript, and browser worker orchestration.
Auto Detect is the default breach mode and runs in the browser worker without app/api routes.
Dual-use security boundary is documented: local educational analysis only, no remote attack automation, no bundled large cracking wordlists.
Design anchor is a forensic spectrum analyzer console with signal-lock progress motion and semantic measurement colors.
Autokey Cipher encryption and decryption with a user-provided key is the grading-safe core path.
Breach Mode now targets classroom demos for Caesar, Reverse, Vigenere, Autokey, Monoalphabetic, Column, toy RSA, toy ElGamal, and JWT locally.
Run history is browser-local through localStorage; there is still no login, database, or custom backend.

lastAchievements: Scaffolded a no-backend Breach Workspace UI with a browser Web Worker, Caesar demo analysis, and JWT decode demo.
Upgraded analysis from common-word-only scoring to IoC, frequency chi-square, trigram and quadgram hints, language markers, and auto-detect family ranking.
Added deterministic Autokey encrypt/decrypt logic with visible keystream output.
Redesigned the first workspace into an Autokey Core plus Breach Console instrument layout.
Implemented bounded local solvers/auditors for Reverse, Vigenere, Autokey breach, Monoalphabetic hill climbing, Column permutation, RSA small-prime factoring, and ElGamal tiny-group discrete log.
Added browser-local run history with clear action and no account or backend dependency.
Updated project, flow, API, data, algorithm, and design docs for the hybrid Autokey plus classroom breach suite direction.
pendingIssues: English and Indonesian quadgram data sources and licenses still need validation.
Classical breach results remain heuristic and work best on classroom-sized, sufficiently long ciphertext.
nextBestActions: Replace lightweight ngram hints with licensed English and Indonesian quadgram tables.
Tune demo fixtures so every class algorithm has a reliable presentation path.
Add behavior tests for malformed artifacts, worker errors, and result conclusions.
